previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted for assistance with bowel preparation ahead of an EGD and colonoscopy due to dysphagia and a history of colonic polyps. During admission, she was found to have esophageal candidiasis on EGD, which was treated with fluconazole. Due to a known drug interaction, her tacrolimus dose was temporarily reduced in coordination with the transplant team. She also developed acute kidney injury and acute diastolic heart failure, likely due to dehydration from bowel prep and recent diuretic use, which improved with IV fluids and a dose of IV Lasix. Her Lasix dose was adjusted post-discharge. She remained stable, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans for medication monitoring and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
#SOB/LETHARGY- On arrival to the floor  Ms. ___ was 
complaining of worsening lethargy, shortness of breath and 
orthopnea.   An EKG on arrival showed Sinus rhythm with left 
ventricular hypertrophy and strain pattern. These findings were 
consistent with past EKG's. Her symptoms of worsening fatigue, 
lethargy, shortness of breath and lower extremity swelling along 
with a newly elevated BNP X2 led us to believe that she may be 
in an acute CHF exacerbation. After discussion with her PCP, ___. 
___ also was concerned about a cardiac cause 
precipitating her current medical decline, it was decided to 
order a pharmacologic stress test.  The stress test showed 
severe left ventricular enlargement with mild systolic 
dysfunction and a LVEF of 41%. She was diuresed with 40mg IV 
furosemide. Her shortness of breath resolved and she felt a 
little more awake then when she arrived on admission. After 
discussion with Dr. ___ considering the immune suppressed 
state of this transplant patient, it was felt that the best 
course of action would be to discharge her because of her high 
suseptability for hospital acquired infection. We sent her home 
on an increased dose of furosemide 80mg BID.   

#PRURITUS- According to Ms. ___ this was not the first time 
she has experienced pruritus. She claims to have these episodes 
approximately every 6 months.  Her laboratory results showed 
normal levels of uric acid and bilirubin. No evidence of rash 
was present on physical exam.  It is unclear at the time of 
discharge as to the cause of this pruritus. It maybe due to 
diabetic neuropathy of which she also suffers from in her lower 
extremity.  

#IMMUNOSUPPRESSION- The transplant team was made aware of this 
patient as soon as she arrived to the floor. Per their request 
she was kept on her home immunosupression regimen of Rapamune, 
Tacrolimus and Prednisone during this short hospital admission.

#TRANSITIONAL- Ms. ___ was instructed to call Dr. ___ 
office to schedule an appointment for follow up within the next 
week.  Dr. ___ will address her newly diagnosed systolic 
dysfunction as an out patient per her request.
